nsr: Rate 60–100, regular, an upright P before every QRS in II, PR 0.12–0.20 s and a narrow QRS.
sbrady: A normal sinus P–QRS–T in every beat, regular, at a rate under 60.
stach: An upright P before every narrow QRS, regular, at 100–150.
svt: Narrow, regular and fast (usually 150–250) with no visible P waves.
af: Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response
Irregularly irregular narrow QRS complexes, no P waves, and a wavy (fibrillatory) baseline, best seen in V1.
flutter: Sawtooth flutter waves at about 300/min (best in II, III, aVF and V1) with a regular ventricular rate of about 150.
vt: Wide (≥ 0.12 s), regular and fast with uniform QRS complexes; P waves march through independently (AV dissociation).
chb: Third-degree (complete) AV block with a ventricular escape
P waves at a normal rate march through without any fixed PR; a slow, wide, regular escape rhythm.
b21: Every other P wave conducts with a constant PR; the dropped P waves sit between the QRS complexes. The QRS is wide (bundle branch block), so suspect Mobitz II.
paced: A pacer spike before every QRS, followed by a wide, LBBB-like complex.
antstemi: ST elevation in V1–V4 (≥ 2 mm in V2–V3) with reciprocal changes: an LAD occlusion.
